trigger: a reader of result_set_routes.hpp trusting the SUCCESS bullet as describing all 4 mutating routes uniformly

Delete/create have no such gap.
classification: truth (comment omission), verified by line-by-line trace not sampling

severity_native: n/a (supporting-context claim, not a finding at time of report)

trigger: a future edit to try_persist_audit that removes its current throw-safety guarantee
summary: rest_api_v1.cpp's deny_fleet_wide_service_scoped (a separate, independent deny-implementation for the same result-set resource, used by GET /api/v1/result-sets/{id}) audits BEFORE setting res.status=403, inverting the documented convention (auth_routes.cpp's deny_service_scoped_session, preflight_routes.hpp, guardian_routes.cpp all audit-AFTER-403, explicitly so a throwing audit sink can't suppress the 403). Not a live bug today since try_persist_audit is itself throw-safe, but a convention drift on the one sibling deny-helper for this resource family.
classification: convention-drift, pre-existing, out of this PR's scope (rest_api_v1.cpp untouched by the extraction)

trigger: a future edit to one of the two independently-typed literal copies of the same denial message without updating the other

classification: minor duplication, too small to warrant a tracked issue on its own
disposition: no-action (below the bar for a tracked issue)

trigger: a service-scoped token hits any of the 6 result-set fragment routes
summary: deny_service_scoped_fn's 403 is application/json, but these 6 routes serve HTML fragments consumed by hx-* swaps; HTMX doesn't swap on non-2xx by default, so a denied service-scoped caller sees no visible UI change. The deny itself is correct (not a security gap) -- UX confusion only. Shared across every module using this closure, not unique to this PR.
classification: UX gap, pre-existing, shared across the closure's other callers too
disposition: no-action (below the bar for a tracked issue; shared/pre-existing UX characteristic of the whole deny_service_scoped_session family)

trigger: a caller probing IDs they don't own, or a transient DB blip, on any of the 4 id-bearing routes (detail/pin/unpin/delete)
summary: rs_get_owned's fail-closed fold (not-found/not-owned/DbError all -> nullopt) means NONE of the 4 id-bearing routes' ownership-check failures are audited -- the only audited denial on this surface is the separate, earlier deny_service_scoped_fn gate. A repeated-probing or transient-degrade pattern leaves zero audit trail.
classification: compliance/evidence gap, distinct from the doc-accuracy finding already fixed

trigger: a result set expires (TTL/GC) or is deleted after being created with a parent_id/large member set
provenance: pre-existing, REST-wide (not scoped to this module)

Once a set expires/deletes, the audit trail is the only remaining lineage record for a documented product-differentiator feature.

trigger: a delete-on-pinned-set failure, observed by on-call outside the requesting browser session

On-call has no machine-readable way to observe a delete silently no-op'd. Folded into the same follow-up issue as the ownership-audit-gap finding (same file/component, same theme).

trigger: an agentic MCP client attempting to author or manage a result set's lifecycle
summary: No MCP tool exposes result-set create/list/pin/unpin/delete/lineage/members -- REST v1 has a comprehensive twin (checked kTools[] name list, confirmed empty for this surface). Scope walking is classified core/mechanism under ADR-1005 Decision 2's own tiebreaker, so the REST+MCP twin obligation applies in full, and no A5 exception-ledger entry covers this gap.
classification: ADR-1005 capability-parity gap, pre-existing, not introduced or worsened by a route-relocation PR
